free_tier.stated: 200 MB hard per package: 'NOTE: 200MB is the maximum size of a package on the Chocolatey Community Repository. The package must download larger tools from a vendor site or mirror, or if possible, create semi-embedded packages.'

retention.stated: per-object-cap: 200 MB per .nupkg. retention: indefinite for moderated packages; unlisted packages remain downloadable

egress.terms: Free serving, but every package is human-moderated before publication (CPMR rule set, VirusTotal scanning).

record.tooling: `choco push` (write, needs API key), `choco install/download` (read), NuGet v2 OData at community.chocolatey.org/api/v2/. No rclone backend.
record.chaining: unlimited packages x unlimited versions x 200 MB, but each package is virus-scanned and moderated. The 2 GB NuGet limitation means large content must be fetched at install time from elsewhere - which is the opposite of storage.
record.limits_note: per-object-cap: 200 MB per .nupkg. retention: indefinite for moderated packages; unlisted packages remain downloadable. request-rate: push is rate-limited per API key; moderation queue is the real gate.
record.reliability_note: 200 MB plus mandatory malware scanning plus human moderation. Cannot hold large binaries at all - Chocolatey's own docs route >2 GB content to external hosting.

evidence.proved: '200MB is the maximum size of a package on the Chocolatey Community Repository.'
'Chocolatey is built on top of NuGet, which itself does not gracefully handle packages that contain files over 2GB'
probe: GET -> 200, 408 bytes (NuGet v2 OData service document live)
